evidence: The 3-D texture read (nebula3d.analysis.fill_texture; GET /api/volumes/{id}/texture and webbridge.volume_texture_json through nebula3d.server.volumes.volume_texture, src/nebula3d/server/volumes.py:505-510) judged a volume's fills wherever the median hole left its rim room: the grid's nodes 2·(median reach + RIM) voxels apart or more (src/nebula3d/analysis/bragg_fill_texture.py:242, :249; RIM = 4, :147; applied at :411). The rule's premise is that a rim on its node's side of the midpoint reads the diffuse falling away from that node. Since #83 (review finding G2) the punch's node test judges no node whose background shell holds under 8 measured voxels (src/nebula3d/analysis/bragg.py:311, :1888), leaves it to the search pass and says so in its record (node_test.notice, src/nebula3d/pipeline.py:1405-1421, :1644). The holes are then the search's peaks, punched to their own measured width (bragg.py:1426), not the node test's footprints at the 0.52 Å⁻¹ cap (profile_max_radius_q 0.5 plus the margin, bragg.py:627), and smaller: the room rule passes where the rim still cannot read the node's own diffuse. Measured on 1045a81 (the validation's synthetic dev cases, the default pipeline): at n=81 (0.161 Å⁻¹ a voxel; the node test's shell needs ≤ 0.143 Å⁻¹) every dev case's record carries the notice. Seven cases' median hole reaches 2 voxels (12 needed, the nodes 10 apart: not judged), but dev-coverage, whose counts end at 4.511 Å⁻¹ before the higher nodes, keeps the 8 (111) and 6 (200) Bragg nodes and the origin: holes of 27, 31 and 9 voxels reaching 1, 2 and 1, the median 1, so 2·(1 + 4) = 10, and the read judged its fills and found a systematic bias above (0.517σ and 0.206 of the level, 14 of the 15 holes above: every limit just passed). Its rims rise away from 14 of the 15 holes (the shell means about the (111) nodes 0.110, 0.105, 0.127 and 0.173 from s = 1 to 4): 4 voxels deep, the rim spans 0.2 to 0.5 r.l.u. from the node, across the noise-free diffuse's minimum (0.25 to 0.35 r.l.u.) and its rise toward the next nodes, so the trend's value at the hole's edge sits 0.03 to 0.04 below the measured first shell and fills at that shell's level read as a bias. Against the case's truth (the noise-free diffuse the validation scores on) the fills are 0.06 to 0.18 below it, not above. At n=161 (no notice) those rims span 0.15 to 0.3 r.l.u. and rise away from 0 to 2 % of the holes on the eight cases (82 to 99 % at n=81), and every dev case is judged, without a bias. The Pilot reads a reason as a grid too coarse by its opening words (web/src/llm/metrics/coarse.ts:11).
proposed_fix: (B) The 3-D read takes the punch's node-test notice as its own "grid too coarse": where the punch's record carries node_test.notice, judge_fill_bias gives not_judged "grid too coarse (the punch's node test could not resolve the holes at this grid)" (NODE_TEST_TOO_COARSE, opening with GRID_TOO_COARSE, so isTooCoarse reads it) and no verdict, before the room rule, the holes and the summary measured as before. The notice is read from the record (nebula3d.pipeline.read_node_test_notice; fill_texture and judge_fill_bias take it as node_test_notice): its limit, the node test's 8-voxel shell floor, is not recomputed, and no limit is added. Weighed and left: (A) the room rule's boundary made strict, a rim shell on the midpoint counted as past it, which the room rule's tests pin as judged in Python and TypeScript and which holes reaching half a voxel at n=81 would pass again; (C) not judged where most rims rise away from their holes, a new share and a question for the user (whether a sound diffuse may dip at the nodes); a quantile of the reach for its median, tuned to the dev cases (19.9 against 20 at n=161); and a test expectation or a known limit, which would leave a coarse-grid artefact as a verdict.
